comparator.name: Pharmacy
comparator.sourceNotes: The Pharmacy major combines a shared first year, a second year of pharmaceutical science, and advanced study of medicines and pharmaceutical practice. It includes a 15 EC research project and 15 EC of restricted Pharmacy electives. Teaching includes both English- and Dutch-language courses.
components: Medicines Group: Drugs for the Central Nervous System
This course also leads to a certificate in safe microbiological techniques.
Requires at least 130 EC four weeks before the project starts.
Medicines Group: Drugs for the Circulatory System
Medicines Group: Drugs for the Endocrine, Digestive and Respiratory System
Medicines Group: Drugs for Infectious Diseases and Oncology

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic bachelor Pharmacy. The 2026-2027 TER offers Major Pharmacy and Major Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences. Major Pharmacy is the eponymous route, contains the programme's full compulsory pharmaceutical-care and drug-science sequence, and is the route that directly reflects the target's broad professional and scientific identity. It is therefore selected independently of UCR fit; the alternative MPS major is a research-oriented route with a 30-EC free minor.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease, pharmacology & biomedical research
alternatives.concept: Study how medicines act by connecting cell biology, biochemistry and physiology with drug targets, metabolism, immunity and disease. Use laboratory work, statistics and research reviews to assess biomedical evidence about treatment.
alternatives.labelReason: Cell biology, biochemistry, physiology and disease mechanisms support the central study of pharmacology. Laboratory and statistical work develop ways to investigate and evaluate evidence.
progression: Cell biology, physiology and biochemistry support later study of drug action, immunity and disease. Programming and data work build toward predictive modelling, and experimental statistics precede evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Medicine use, health behaviour & public health
alternatives.concept: Connect the study of medicines and disease with health behaviour, patient experience and public health. Use epidemiology, health psychology and evidence reviews to explore treatment decisions, and examine how communication, access and public policy shape them.
alternatives.labelReason: Pharmacology, physiology and disease establish the biomedical context. Health psychology, epidemiology and public economics address decisions, access and the social context of care.
progression: Life science, brain and behaviour, and epidemiology support later work in physiology, pharmacology, disease and health psychology. Quantitative and qualitative research methods precede evidence synthesis.
alternatives.distinctness: The options differ by 12 courses and 90 EC each way. The biomedical option emphasises cell biology, biochemistry, laboratory work, immunity and quantitative modelling. The medicine-use option emphasises psychology, qualitative inquiry, communication and public economics.

core: Molecular and cellular disease, physiology and biological drug targets
Pharmacology, medicine action, safety, effectiveness, side effects and interactions
Pharmaceutical chemistry, analysis, formulation, delivery and manufacture
Biomedical laboratory study of cells, molecules and disease
Mathematics, statistics, epidemiology and evidence evaluation
Research ethics, medicine safety and responsible use
Patient-centred pharmaceutical care, communication and professional responsibility
adjacent: Biomedical drug mechanisms and disease research
Patient-centred medicine use, health behaviour and communication
questions: How do medicines act on biological targets and disease processes?
How can medicine safety, effectiveness, sustainability and cost-effectiveness be evaluated?
How do patient behaviour, communication and social context shape medicine use?

candidates.label: Medicine use, health behaviour & public health
Drug discovery, pharmaceutical chemistry & formulation
candidates.assessment: UCR has biochemistry and pharmacology but no cumulative chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, dosage-form technology, biopharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, organic synthesis, drug design or formulation-and-delivery sequence. A third programme would misrepresent general life-science and data courses as pharmaceutical development training.

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible: one centred on molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical evidence, and one centred on medicine use, health behaviour and patient context. The next generator-backed direction is drug discovery, chemistry and formulation; UCR cannot implement it, so production stops at two and preserves the specialist and professional gaps explicitly.

blocks: Both study the functions and regulation of human organ systems.

Both study mechanisms of disease across human organ systems.
Both examine immune mechanisms and inflammation. Groningen studies these mechanisms in relation to medicines.
Both develop practical biological laboratory skills. UCR also covers microbiology and protein work.
Groningen introduces pharmaceutical dosage forms and their behaviour in the body.
Groningen develops laboratory methods for analysing pharmaceutical substances.
This course includes the Groningen certificate in safe microbiological techniques.
Groningen continues formulation and biopharmacy in a second course.
Groningen studies how molecular properties affect a substance’s potential as a medicine.
Both use statistical inference to interpret empirical results. UCR emphasises experimental design and behavioural research.
Both use population study designs and examine bias and risk. Groningen applies these methods to the use and effects of medicines.
Groningen devotes a full course to pharmacokinetics. UCR introduces kinetics within Pharmacology.

notes.text: The Groningen major combines drug science with pharmaceutical care and professional practice. The UCR options explore biomedical drug mechanisms or the social and behavioural context of medicine use.

UCR Pharmacology introduces drug action and pharmacokinetics. The UCR options lack Groningen’s specialist courses in drug formulation, pharmaceutical analysis and medicinal chemistry, as well as its training in pharmacy practice.

audience.programmeDescription: Pharmacy at Groningen studies how medicines are developed, how they act in the body and how they are used in patient care. The comparison follows the Pharmacy major.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options focus on the biology of drug action or on how people and health systems make treatment decisions. Groningen also teaches the preparation and analysis of medicines and pharmaceutical care.
